Monday to Saturday

Six-day gym plan

Weeks 1–2: two light sets per exercise. Finish each set with 3–4 good reps still in reserve. Never train to failure yet, and ask a trainer to show each machine's setup.

Every session

  1. Warm up 5 minutes on treadmill or bike.
  2. Arm circles, shoulder rolls, hip mobility.
  3. Do the exercises with slow, controlled reps.
  4. Rest 60–90 seconds between sets, longer if needed.
  5. Cool down with 3–5 minutes of easy walking.

Vegetarian · eggs · whey

Meal plan

A new combination every week, so no two weeks repeat the same menu. Weights are cooked unless marked dry. Protein figures are approximate.

Week 1

Snacks

Mid-morning · 10:30

Apple + 200 g Greek yogurt, or guava + milk, or orange + 30 g roasted chana.

Pre-workout · 4:30

Banana + black coffee, or banana + milk, or 2 idlis + sambar.

Before bed, optional

Milk or plain curd if you're hungry or short on protein.

The rotation doesn't automatically hit 2,100–2,200 kcal or 140 g protein every day. Top up with whey, milk or curd, and check your brands' labels. If you have allergies or medical diet needs, adapt it with a dietitian.
Cook it right

Recipe book

Tap a recipe for the steps. Photos are for inspiration; your real serving is the measured portion.

Breakfast · 5 min + overnight

Protein overnight oats

60 g oats250 ml milk1 scoop whey½–1 banana5 g chia
  1. Add oats, milk and chia to a sealed container.
  2. Mix, cover and refrigerate overnight.
  3. In the morning, stir in the whey. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
  4. Top with banana. Keep nuts measured; they add calories quickly.

Add whey after soaking for a smoother texture.

Breakfast · 12–15 min

Paneer bhurji + whole-wheat toast

150 g paneer1 onion1 tomato½ capsicum2 toast slices
  1. Heat a measured teaspoon of oil; sauté onion and capsicum.
  2. Add tomato, turmeric, chilli, cumin and coriander powder.
  3. Crumble in the paneer and cook 3–4 minutes.
  4. Finish with coriander; serve with toast and cucumber.

Lower-fat paneer cuts calories; check the pack for protein and fat.

Breakfast · 20 min

Moong dal chilla with paneer

80 g dry moong75 g paneerGinger + chilliCurd on the side
  1. Soak moong 4–6 hours or overnight; drain.
  2. Blend with ginger, chilli, cumin, salt and water to a pourable batter.
  3. Spread thin on a non-stick tawa; cook both sides with minimal oil.
  4. Add crumbled paneer, fold, serve with curd and mint chutney.

Soak extra dal only if you will use it within a day or two.

Lunch · 25–30 min

Rajma rice + curd bowl

200 g cooked rajma150 g cooked rice150–200 g curdSalad
  1. Soak dry rajma overnight; discard the water and rinse.
  2. Pressure-cook until completely soft. Never eat undercooked kidney beans.
  3. Simmer with onion-tomato masala, ginger, garlic and spices.
  4. Serve measured rajma and rice with curd and a big salad.

Cook a batch, portion it, refrigerate or freeze; reheat thoroughly.

Lunch / dinner · 20 min

Soya chunk masala

50–60 g dry soya1 onion1 tomato2 rotis or rice
  1. Boil soya chunks 5–7 minutes; drain, rinse, squeeze out water.
  2. Cook onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices in measured oil.
  3. Add soya and a little water; simmer 6–8 minutes.
  4. Serve with measured rice or rotis, vegetables and curd.

Check the pack for protein per 100 g; brands differ.

Dinner · 15–20 min

Paneer & tofu vegetable bowl

200 g tofu or paneer200 g mixed vegSoy sauceRice portion
  1. Pat tofu dry and cube it; use a non-stick pan.
  2. Brown it lightly in a measured teaspoon of oil.
  3. Add beans, capsicum, carrot and broccoli; stir-fry until just tender.
  4. Season with garlic, pepper, lemon and a little low-sodium soy sauce.

Firm tofu holds its shape; use its label to count protein.

Dinner · 20 min

Simple egg curry + roti

3 eggs1 onion1 tomato2 rotisCurd + veg
  1. Boil eggs fully, cool and peel.
  2. Make an onion-tomato masala with ginger, garlic and spices.
  3. Add water for gravy; simmer the eggs 4–5 minutes.
  4. Serve with 2 medium rotis, vegetables and curd.

For a fully vegetarian day, swap eggs for tofu or soya.

Pre-workout · 2 min

Simple gym fuel

1 bananaBlack coffee, optionalWater
  1. Eat a banana 30–60 minutes before training if it suits your stomach.
  2. Drink water. Skip coffee if it affects sleep or digestion.
  3. If hungry, have 2 idlis with sambar or banana with milk.

Don't try a new supplement or big meal right before training.

Higher-protein snacks

Greek yogurt or hung curd with fruit; milk with whey; paneer cubes with cucumber.

Budget-friendly

Roasted chana + curd; boiled chana chaat; sprouts with lemon and curd.

Before the gym

Banana; banana + milk; 2 idlis + sambar. Keep it light and familiar.

Meal timing

Protein

Eggs, paneer, tofu, soya chunks, dal, rajma, chana, Greek yogurt, curd, whey.

Carbs

Rice, roti, oats, idli, fruit, potatoes. Measure portions; rice is fine.

Vegetables and fats

Vegetables at lunch and dinner. Measure oil, nuts, seeds and chutneys.

Weekly

Grocery list

Tick items as they go in the bag.

Sunday meal prep

  1. Wash and chop vegetables.
  2. Cook a batch of dal or rajma and refrigerate promptly.
  3. Portion dry oats, nuts and seeds.
  4. Make overnight oats for Monday.
  5. Keep paneer, tofu, curd and eggs stocked.
  6. Pack lunch boxes for the first workdays.
  7. Don't leave cooked rice or other cooked food at room temperature for hours. Reheat thoroughly.
Read once

Beginner rules and safety

How to start gym · 6 steps (Eshwar Bolegar)
  1. Choose a gym you can reach every day.
  2. Pick one goal: for you, fat loss to your goal weight.
  3. Get proper guidance: follow Cherry's coach and ask the trainer to check your form.
  4. Eat a proper diet: your targets and meal plan in Nutrition.
  5. Stay consistent: protect your gym streak.
  6. Check progress weekly: the weekly review and your 7-day average.

In the gym

  • Start with the lightest practical weight.
  • Ask the trainer to set seats, pads and handles with you.
  • Move slowly; no momentum.
  • Keep breathing; don't hold your breath.
  • Stop if a movement causes sharp pain.
  • Don't double up to make up missed sessions.

Recovery

  • Sleep 7–9 hours.
  • Keep Sunday for recovery.
  • Build steps gradually: 6k, 7k, 8k, then 8.5–9k.
  • Soreness is normal; sharp or worsening pain is not.
  • Ease off if you're unusually tired or getting weaker.

Supplements

WheyOptional, convenient protein. Use the label's serving size.
CreatineOptional monohydrate, 3–5 g daily, no loading phase. Check with a doctor first if you have kidney problems or other medical conditions.
B12 · Vitamin DDiscuss testing and dose with a doctor or dietitian.
Fat burnersAvoid.
